source: tool-usage brief: our own tool tracking (30 days, data_days 27) + 7 live persona walkthroughs + queued tool specs
interpretedBrief: Real visitors used seven ModernWallet calculators (Florida Amendment 3, inflation, Social Security taxable benefits, self-employment set-aside, stock capital gains, long-term care cost, probate vs trust). Fix what blocked them in their walkthroughs, add books under the result where a book fits the result, and build the next tools a mortgage-tool user reaches for (biweekly payments; pay off or invest), which earlier runs specced twice.

actions.problem: florida-amendment-3-calculator (67 people, 71 uses, 142 views; data_days 27). Walkthrough: the result says 'if Amendment 3 passes' though voters approved it Nov 3, 2026 (page FAQ says so); homes assessed $25,000-$76,411 get a flat $51,411 exemption instead of the banded one (Fla. Const. Art. VII s.6(a), s. 196.031(1)(b) F.S.), so a $60,000 home at 11.2 mills shows $96 saved instead of $280; no newcomer input; 0 millage gives a silent $0. Evidence: reports/tool-usage-pass/2026-11-04/personas/florida-amendment-3-calculator.md
actions.solution: In src/lib/florida-amendment-3.ts compute today's exemption as 25,000 + clamp(assessed - 50,000, 0, 26,411) (2027/2028 and homes >= $76,411 unchanged; regression cases $60,000 -> $280, $45,000 -> $224); in src/components/FloridaAmendment3Calculator.tsx change the sub-line to 'approved by voters Nov 3, 2026', add a 'Florida resident with homestead on Dec 31, 2026?' Yes/No toggle (default Yes; No keeps the current exemption for 2027-2028 with the fifth-year note) and a zero-millage hint.

newPageBriefs.takeaway: Prepay when the after-tax return you can count on is below the break-even rate the calculator shows; invest when your mortgage rate is low or the money goes into a tax-free account; keep an emergency fund first, because prepaid principal is hard to get back.
